fieldMarks: The only marsupial north of Mexico
Whitish underfur tipped with black; coloration varies across the range
Robust body, short legs and an opposable thumb-like hind toe; about 1.9–2.8 kg
behavior: Nocturnal and solitary, active dusk to dawn; does not hibernate but is less active in the coldest weather
When threatened adults hiss, bare teeth or flee; feigning death is mostly by young animals
Opportunistic omnivore: small animals, insects, worms, fruit and seeds
Somewhat nomadic, often staying in an area only months
habitat: Varied, from dry country to wet meadows, but prefers woodlands and thickets near water.
range: Most of the eastern and central U.S. and adjacent southeastern Canada (north into Ontario), west to South Dakota, Colorado and Arizona; introduced on the Pacific coast and into British Columbia, and still expanding north and west.
